objective: Exploratory census with a frozen contract: the Vamos matroid as the free-set family of a support relation and of a union of two GF(7) codes, and failures in their laws; random laws of subgroups over Z4, Z9, S3, D5 and AGL(1,5), whose systems' free sets should equal those of their images in the product of top quotients, with no circuit mixing top primes; and every single-tuple perturbation of x+y+z=0 over Z3 and of its lift with 2 doubled, each either failing or keeping the Z3 law's constrained sets.
status: Closed: supported by MATROID-CONVERSE-20261021-001A-E001 (exploratory; Q1-Q5 hold and all four controls pass; the independent check rebuilt every witness, re-solved every recorded group system with its own group code plus 20 fresh ones per group, and re-decided the survivors on fresh systems). The Vamos matroid is exactly the free-set family of its support relation and of a union of two GF(7) codes, and both relations' circuit projections have direct cases whose two copies fail. In 750 systems over random subgroup laws of Z4, Z9, S3, D5 and AGL(1,5), every free-set family was a matroid equal to that of the system's image in its tops, with no circuit mixing top primes (two primes present in 80 systems). x+y+z=0 over Z6 failed and over Z3 did not. Of 91 single-tuple perturbations of x+y+z=0 over Z3 and of its lift with 2 doubled, 83 failed and the 8 survivors, exactly the removals from the lift's (2,2,2)-block, kept the Z3 law's constrained sets in every sampled system.
title: Census: Vamos in relations, tops in group laws, perturbations of a difference law
